questions.question: The capital account and the current account differ in that:
options: Capital holds the long-term investment and barely moves; the current account receives profit shares and gives up drawings every year
Capital changes monthly; the current account never changes
The current account holds the loan from the bank

questions.question: A DEBIT balance on a partner's current account means:
options: The partner has drawn more than earned — the partner owes the business

questions.question: Partners' salaries and interest on capital are:
options: APPROPRIATIONS — divisions of a profit already made, after the net profit line

questions.question: The partnership agreement governs:
options: Only the opening of the bank account
Salaries for working, interest for waiting capital, any bonus, and the ratio for the remainder

subtopics.title: Dividing the Profit — the Appropriation Account

questions.question: After salaries R168 000, interest R30 000 and the bonus R12 000, the remainder of the R240 000 profit is:
options: R30 000, shared equally at R15 000 each

questions.question: The proof that the division is correct is that:
options: Both partners receive the same total
Zola's R131 000 plus Sipho's R109 000 equals exactly the R240 000 profit — the account EMPTIES
The bank balance equals the profit

questions.question: Interest on capital at 10% gives:
options: R10 000 to Zola and R20 000 to Sipho
Zola R20 000 on R200 000 and Sipho R10 000 on R100 000

questions.question: Sipho's current account — opening debit 6 000, share 109 000, drawings 95 000 — closes at:
options: R8 000 credit — he cleared last year's overdraw and the business now owes him

subtopics.title: The Statements, the Notes and the Asset That Left

questions.question: The disposal's four steps, in order, are:
options: Cost out to Disposal; accumulated depreciation out to Disposal; record the proceeds; the difference is profit or loss
Proceeds first, then cost, then depreciation
Only the carrying value is transferred

questions.question: The vehicle costing R80 000 with accumulated depreciation R50 000, sold for R35 000, produces:
options: A profit of R5 000 — proceeds 35 000 against carrying value 30 000

questions.question: The statement of financial position totals:
options: R503 000 — assets 335 000 plus 168 000, financed by equity 333 000, loan 100 000 and current liabilities 70 000

questions.question: The capital and current account notes exist so that:
options: Each partner can verify their own treatment — every salary, interest, bonus, share and drawing in their own column

questions.question: Debtors collection of two months against thirty-day terms means:
options: Money is resting in customers' pockets — collection is slow and needs tightening

questions.question: The gearing reading of 0,3 : 1 says:
options: Lightly geared — one rand of loan for every three of equity; room to borrow for expansion

questions.question: The honest footnote on the 75% return on average equity is:
options: Partners' salaries sit INSIDE it — it rewards their labour as well as their capital
It cannot be compared to anything

questions.question: Matching indicators to the eye that watches them:
options: The partner asks liquidity; the creditor asks return
All eyes watch only net profit
The creditor asks liquidity, the lender asks gearing, the partner asks return

subtopics.title: Two Friends, One Till, and the Paper That Keeps the Peace

questions.question: The two dangerous sentences every partnership fight comes from are:
options: "I put in more, so more is mine" and "I work harder, so more is mine"
"Prices are too low" and "rent is too high"
"The bank is slow" and "the till is broken"

questions.question: The agreement answers both sentences with:
options: A salary for the one who works, interest for the money that waits, and a ratio for whatever remains — written and signed

questions.question: The pile that moves every year is:
options: The LIVING pile — the current account, receiving the profit share and giving up the drawings

questions.question: The ladles empty the pot in the order:
options: Wages for work; thanks to the waiting money; the promised bonus; the agreed split of the rest

questions.question: "The pot is empty, to the rand" matters because:
options: Appropriation never creates or loses a cent — it only divides; plates totalling the pot prove the division
The pot must show a loss

questions.question: The "two rooms" the exam always checks are:
options: Expenses before the profit line; sharing after it — partner salaries live in the second room

questions.question: "The friends are quietly lending their customers money" refers to:
options: Debtors taking two months to pay against thirty-day terms
Stock turning six times a year

questions.question: The creditor sleeps easy because:
options: Near money covers near debt at 2,4 to one — and one to one even without selling stock

questions.question: Stock turning six times a year means:
options: Stock is thrown away every two months
The shelves empty and refill about every two months — stock is alive, not a museum

questions.question: The scoreboard way of reading any number is:
options: Trust it if it is large
Convert it to a percentage always
Never alone — against last year, against the terms, against the bank — then judge
